title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
abstract: arXiv:2610.27227v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill. Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit. We present \textbf{GRSE}, \textbf{G}roup-\textbf{R}elative \textbf{S}kill \textbf{E}volution, which assigns behavioral credit by comparison: inspired by GRPO, it executes each question several times under the same skill libraries and contrasts the executions to credit agent--skill pairs, with structured diagnosis of failures. On HotpotQA and LoCoMo with two open-weight actors, GRSE outperforms MASkills, the closest prior method, on HotpotQA and every LoCoMo category except open-domain, with the largest gains on multi-hop questions ($+6.7$ and $+3.2$ F1). Its gains rest on better-grounded retrieval

translated_title: 哪个智能体的技能需要改变？面向多智能体团队进化的组相对信用分配方法
translated_abstract: 合作型语言模型智能体可以通过修订可复用的技能来在不更新权重的情况下持续改进，但前提是必须将共享的团队奖励追溯到应负责任的智能体与技能。现有方法对每条轨迹中出现的技能给予信用，然而“出现”并不等于“责任”：在成功运行中被激活的有害技能依然会获得正向信用。我们提出了GRSE（组相对技能进化，Group-Relative Skill Evolution），它通过比较来分配行为信用：受GRPO启发，该方法在相同的技能库下对每个问题执行多次，并对比这些执行结果来为智能体-技能对分配信用，同时对失败进行结构化诊断。在使用两个开源权重模型于HotpotQA和LoCoMo数据集上的实验中，GRSE在最接近的先前方法MASkills之上，在HotpotQA以及除开放域外的所有LoCoMo类别上均表现更优，其中在多跳问题上增益最大（+6.7和+3.2 F1）。其增益源于更可靠的检索基础。
tldr: GRSE受GRPO启发，通过在相同技能库下多次执行同一问题并进行组内对比，将团队奖励精准追溯到具体的智能体-技能对，解决了“技能出现不等于技能责任”的信用分配难题，显著提升了多智能体协作性能。
